governing_correction: Responsibility state cost depends on registered decision semantics. V1 full-optimal-action-set signatures are stronger than necessary for ANY_OPTIMAL_ACTION responsibilities.

claims.claim: The complete-linguistic-future predictive quotient S_P is the minimal exact predictive state under the stated finite assumptions.
A state sufficient for linguistic prediction may be insufficient for a distinct task/responsibility target.

A Machine-Epistemic responsibility is decision-relative and must specify target Q, admissible actions, loss, and exact decision semantics rather than treating arbitrary Q recovery as the universal state requirement.
For ANY_OPTIMAL_ACTION, exact additional deterministic state entropy beyond retained S_P is min over Bayes-optimal selectors d of H(d(H)|S_P).
For CANONICAL_ACTION with registered selector d_tau, exact additional state entropy is H(d_tau(H)|S_P).
For OPTIMAL_ACTION_SET, exact additional state entropy is H(A_star(H)|S_P), which can strictly exceed the ANY_OPTIMAL_ACTION cost.
For EXACT_TARGET with deterministic Q and zero-one loss, exact additional state entropy reduces to H(Q|S_P).
For several ANY_OPTIMAL_ACTION responsibilities, the exact joint state cost is the minimum over jointly selected Bayes-optimal policies of H(d_1(H),...,d_m(H)|S_P).
Every entropy-minimal deterministic representation exactly sufficient for the complete linguistic future is almost-surely isomorphic to S_P.

Prediction-preserving maximal compression is safe for a fixed responsibility policy only if that policy is implementable from S_P; otherwise minimal predictive state lacks required action information.
Under log loss, responsibility uncertainty from Z decomposes as H(Q|H)+I(Q;H|Z).
A representation can preserve complete linguistic prediction and a registered current optimal policy while losing information required to update that policy correctly after future observations.

For a fixed registered current/future responsibility policy semantics, the minimal exact recursively updateable state is the coarsest right-congruent refinement of the current predictive-policy label.
For fixed-policy dynamic state, extra exact average state required solely for future update correctness is H(S_infinity|S_0).

The stronger problem that jointly optimizes Bayes-optimal policy selection and recursive state is not solved by the current right-congruence theorem and remains an explicit nonclaim unless separately mechanized.
Prospective log-loss deficiency is I(Q_future;H_now|Z_now,X_future) under the declared joint model.

Responsibility-family state overhead is bounded above by H(H|S_P); a predictive-fibre-separating responsibility family saturates this bound and forces retention of all non-predictive history on support.
Any non-injective state fails some exact binary responsibility; unrestricted exact future responsibility sufficiency therefore admits no nontrivial compression.
Single-responsibility conditional log-loss frontier [H(Q|S_P)-D]_+ and independent product extensions are classical log-loss rate-distortion benchmarks, not independent ORION novelty.
Predictive behavior/static hidden-state probes cannot by themselves certify prospective responsibility-update sufficiency of a real LLM state.
